title: Longitudinal-Field-Driven Transition in a non-integrable Non-Hermitian Transverse-Field Ising Chain via RBMs
authors: M. E. Ateuafack, M. R. Kamsap, J. T. Diffo, L. C. Fai, M. N. Jipdi
abstract: We investigate the ground-state properties and quantum critical behavior of a non-Hermitian transverse-field Ising chain subjected to longitudinal and complex transverse magnetic fields. To address this interacting many-body problem, we employ real-valued neural quantum states based on Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs), optimized using Variational Monte Carlo (VMC) sampling. Spectral analysis of finite chains reveals exceptional points associated with spontaneous parity-time (PT) symmetry breaking. A real-valued RBM framework is developed to reconstruct the ground-state eigenstates of the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. Benchmark comparisons with exact diagonalization demonstrate that the RBM approach accurately reproduces the ground-state energy, magnetization, and spin-spin correlations. Extending the analysis to larger system sizes, we identify a non-Hermitian quantum phase transition characterized by PT-symmetry breaking and the emergence of magnetic order. Our results establish real-valued neural quantum states as an efficient and scalable framework for investigating critical phenomena in interacting non-Hermitian quantum systems.
summary: The authors apply Restricted Boltzmann Machines within a Variational Monte Carlo framework to study a non-Hermitian Ising chain. They successfully map out a longitudinal-field-driven quantum phase transition characterized by spontaneous PT-symmetry breaking and magnetic ordering. This establishes RBMs as an efficient tool for analyzing critical phenomena in complex, interacting open quantum systems.
main_problem: Investigating the ground-state properties and quantum critical behavior of a non-Hermitian transverse-field Ising chain subjected to longitudinal and complex transverse magnetic fields.
main_result: The RBM approach successfully characterizes the PT-symmetry-breaking transition and the emergence of magnetic order in this challenging, interacting non-Hermitian system.
method: The study employs real-valued neural quantum states (NQSs) based on Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs), optimized using Variational Monte Carlo (VMC) sampling to tackle the many-body problem.
model_or_system: The model is a 1D non-Hermitian Transverse-Field Ising Chain governed by a Hamiltonian incorporating transverse, longitudinal ($h$), and complex transverse fields ($\xi$). The system becomes non-integrable due to the longitudinal field.
key_observables: Ground-state energy (real part), magnetization ($M_z$), spin-spin correlation function ($C_{zz}(r)$), and detection of exceptional points (EPs).
important_parameters: Longitudinal field strength ($h$) and the imaginary transverse field parameter ($\xi$). Critical transition occurs around $h_c \approx 0.3$.
main_assumptions: The use of RBMs as a variational ansatz to approximate the ground state, which is necessary because exact diagonalization fails for large systems.
figures_summary: Figures show energy spectra revealing exceptional points (EPs) and track the evolution of the ground-state energy and magnetization across varying longitudinal fields ($h$), confirming phase transitions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the Hamiltonian, develops the RBM-VMC framework for non-Hermitian systems, benchmarks results against ED, and then maps out quantum phase transitions by tracking symmetry breaking (PT) and magnetic order using multiple observables like $C_{zz}(r)$.
why_interesting: This work demonstrates a powerful, scalable numerical technique (RBMs) to analyze complex non-Hermitian dynamics, which is highly relevant for open quantum systems where gain/loss mechanisms are present.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Symmetry breaking and exceptional points obtained with the ED. Energy spectrum of the system for varying longitudinal fields h, illustrating the emergence of exceptional points (EPs). Columns display the real parts (a, d, g), imaginary parts (b, e, h), and the maximum overlap (c, f, i), respectively. Parameters are fixed at N = 4 and η = 0.5, with rows tracking field strengths of h = 0.1 (a–c), h = 0.3 (d–f), and h = 1.0 (g–i).

FIG. 2: Symmetry breaking and exceptional points. Energy spectrum of the system for varying longitudinal fields h, illustrating the emergence of exceptional points (EPs). Columns display the real parts (a, d, g), imaginary parts (b, e, h), and the maximum overlap (c, f, i), respectively. Parameters are fixed at N = 8 and η = 0.5, with rows tracking field strengths of h = 0.1 (a–c), h = 0.3 (d–f), and h = 1.0 (g–i). Band coloring corresponds to their chronological order of appearance.

FIG. 3: Maximum-overlap phase diagram in the (h) −(ξ) parameter space. The yellow regions identify the parameter regimes where exceptional points (EPs) occur, characterized by the coalescence of eigenstates and a maximum overlap equal to unity. The remaining parameters are fixed at N = 4 and η = 0.5.

FIG. 4: RBM vs. exact diagonalisation. (a) Energy variance of the real part of the local energy, and (b) the corresponding ground-state energy of the system as a function of training steps. The Restricted Boltzmann Machine (RBM) successfully converges to the exact ground-state energy predicted by exact diagonalization (indicated by the black dashed line). The variance curve demonstrates that convergence initiates around 200 training steps. The fixed parameters for this simulation are N = 10 , η = 0.5, ξ = 0.05 and h = 0.1.
